repository.name: @webex/plugin-authorization-browser-first-party
repository.purpose: Browser OAuth 2.0 authorization plugin for the first-party Webex Web Client. It registers webex.authorization, completes the Authorization Code + PKCE redirect during SDK initialization (CSRF state check, URL scrubbing, preauth catalog hint, token exchange), starts first-party and third-party (social provider) login redirects, runs the Device Authorization (QR code) polling flow, and supplies public/confidential client authentication for the token exchange and refresh callback.

public_interfaces.name: @webex/plugin-authorization-browser-first-party package barrel
public_interfaces.notes: Importing the package registers Authorization as public plugin 'authorization' with config and the isAuthorizing/isAuthenticating proxies. WebexCore keeps the first registration of a name, so import this package before the webex bundle.

public_interfaces.name: webex.authorization runtime methods, properties, and events
public_interfaces.audience: Webex Web Client sign-in, QR login UI, and WebexCore logout
public_interfaces.notes: Properties: isAuthorizing, isAuthenticating, ready, initialAuthorizationCodeGrantOutcome. Config keys under config.credentials: clientType (default public) and refreshCallback. Events is a module export, not an instance property.

glossary.definition: The access + refresh token bundle stored on webex.credentials after a code or device grant.
glossary.notes: Owned by the webex-core credentials plugin.

glossary.definition: The retained result (not_attempted, success, failure) of the exchange run during plugin initialization only.
glossary.notes: Not reset by logout; not current authorization state.

glossary.definition: clientType 'public': no client secret; client_id is sent in the token form with addAuthHeader false.
glossary.notes: Any other clientType uses HTTP Basic client authentication.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not leave code, id_token, email, or csrf_token in the URL after a callback.
negative_guidance.why: They leak through history, copy-paste, and referrers.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not log authorization codes, tokens, client secrets, or raw emails.
negative_guidance.why: They are credentials or PII; only the email hash may leave the page.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not read a CSRF token or PKCE verifier from sessionStorage without removing it.
Do not treat README.md as the list of methods, events, or event order.
negative_guidance.why: It reads Events from the instance and misstates QR timeout and slow_down behavior. See docs/adr/0001-retain-product-readme.md.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not infer a coverage threshold for this package.
negative_guidance.why: The owner confirmed no coverage gate applies; the legacy Jest config disables coverage collection.

high.expectation: Source and unit test evidence both support the change, and the behavior has a case in test/unit/spec/authorization.js.

medium.expectation: Only source evidence exists, for example plugin registration, 400 grant-error mapping, the logout redirect, or the shared event emitter. Pin current behavior with a characterization test before modifying.

low.expectation: Neither source nor tests settle the question. Stop and report the gap.
